summary: Connects nearby points with 2-point line primitives, either within the first input or between a second input and the first. It can limit distance, line count, duplicate lines, and output line direction, line length, or matched endpoint attributes.

key_params.name: maxlinesperpoint
key_params.note: Maximum lines generated from each point

key_params.name: uniformdist
key_params.note: Distributes selection more uniformly among nearby candidates

key_params.name: maxtempneighbors
key_params.note: Temporary candidate storage before pruning to max line count

key_params.name: duplines
key_params.note: Do nothing, avoid, or delete duplicate line pairs

key_params.name: numhashbuckets
key_params.note: Spatial hash bucket count; often close to point count

key_params.name: output
key_params.note: Output shared-point lines or point primitives

key_params.name: endptattrs
key_params.note: Output endpoint attributes from connected points

key_params.name: origin
key_params.note: Select which endpoint supplies origin-style attributes

key_params.name: remunusedpoints
key_params.note: Remove points that are not referenced by output primitives

key_params.name: cpureadback
key_params.note: Enable CPU readback for diagnostics or CPU consumers

key_concepts: Proximity POP performs neighbor searches within minimum and maximum distance limits and emits 2-point line primitives for selected pairs.
One-input mode connects points within the same set, while a second input lets one point set query nearby points in another set.
Line direction, line length, endpoint attribute, duplicate-line, and unused-point controls turn the neighbor graph into usable downstream attributes.
common_gotchas: Proximity outputs 2-point line primitives, not line strips; use Line Break or other line tools if strip topology is needed.
Spatial hashing performance depends on numhashbuckets; tune it for large point clouds.
When using two inputs, end point attribute output can duplicate substantial data, so scope the attributes carefully.
